title: Is there a Director that, although popular and critically accomplished, you just can't stand?

commenti.body:
Honestly, Tarantino, at least, Tarantino post *Jackie Brown*. His films are just obnoxious and too often feel like he's just getting his rocks off saying/showing things that he thinks are "edgy" and "cool". I enjoy watching them to some extent because he is extremely talented, I just hate a lot of the things they seem to *say* if that makes any sense. 

As for Villeneuve, I can understand people taking that point. I think he's very talented in terms of visual scale and wonder but at the same time his films seem to get obsessed with that to the point of losing their emotional heft. I'm too often left cold. There are exceptions, I think *Enemy* and *Prisoners* are fantastic. I did enjoy *Dune* more the second time, though I feel I was bringing my own emotions... like, I knew what was happening so I sort of inserted them in there.

I also very much dislike Tarantino. It is evident in certain set-pieces of his that he has a somewhat of a talent for writing and direction, and can build a coherent and fine arc within a vacuum, but doing this for the entire runtime of a film doesn't seem to be a capability of his. I think he is quite ill-disciplined, similar to Mathew Vaughn, and that he often loses focus. Most of the time, his films feel like less than the sum of their parts. Sometimes he is just completely tasteless and crass. For the most part, his films are, as someone on this sub put it in the past, very broad stroke, hit you over the head type of films. That they allow people, along with those of Scorsese and Nolan (I think these two are much better), to get into a brand of film that might be considered more—jesus this sound really pretentious—'intellectual', is a good thing, however.

With Villeneuve, I actually really love his work, especially Arrival and Sicario, but was left disappointed by Dune. I will die on the hill of David Lynch's adaptation being far superior and a masterpiece of filmmaking.
